brand.dataResidency: Nothing leaves your machine unless you set IRIS_OTEL_ENDPOINT, which exports traces to the collector you name, or enable the LLM judge with your own key.
brand.discoverySentence: Add the config block, restart your client, and every session lists Iris's tools on connect. Iris never intercepts: it runs when your agent calls one of its tools, when a host hook or `iris-eval ingest` hands it a trace, or when you POST one to its HTTP API.

capabilityMap.about: What Iris can judge, cell by cell: ten evaluation questions against six subjects. `has` means at least one shipped, measured thing answers the question for that subject; `partial` means something answers it with a stated limit; `gap` means nothing does yet; `n/a` means the question does not apply to the subject. Every `has` or `partial` cell names its evidence — a rule, a tool, a resource, a route, a proof row or a judge template — and each name resolves to something registered in this release (tests/capability-map-contract.test.ts). `needs` lists the inputs a call must carry for the cell's rules to judge; without them those rules skip and the verdict's `coverage` says so.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Deterministic detectors for leaked personal data and credentials, injection-shaped output and deployment-prohibited words, each fire naming the pattern and the span; precision and recall are published per rule at https://iris-eval.com/proof, not yet per entity.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: The safety detectors read the output; supplying the input changes nothing for them, so the single-output answer carries over. A keyed judge template for harm potential exists and is unmeasured.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: A directive found in a tool result is related to what the agent did next: no_injection_compliance matches directive wording as literal phrases over a capped, normalised slice — never a regular expression, because a tool result is attacker-controlled — and fails when a later call carries terms the directive introduced and the ask never used. Merely repeating those terms is reported on a passing result, because measured on its own family that weaker signal cannot tell reporting an injection from complying with one.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Safe on nine of ten runs is readable as a case's pass rate over its repeats: compare_traces groups every evaluation of one case across runs and reports the case's pass rate with a 95% Wilson interval and a flaky flag, and the run-level rate by a cluster bootstrap over cases — of the composed verdict, not of this question alone; a per-question filter is not shipped, so the rate cannot be read for this question by itself.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Per-rule failure counts over a time window are served to the dashboard, with no interval and no cohort key.

cells.question: Q1
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The three safety detectors are measured on a labelled corpus with 95% intervals, and every fire carries its positive predictive value at the stated prior; robustness to obfuscated text is not yet measured.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Without an input only two context-free fabrication signals run, and the result says so; the grounded signals need the material the agent was given.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: A deterministic detector with context-grounded contradiction signals, measured with intervals; keyed judge templates for accuracy, correctness against a reference and faithfulness to sources, plus a citation verifier, cover what patterns cannot — on a key the user supplies.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: Tool outputs are read as grounding material: a file, directory or URL the output cites that neither the ask nor anything the agent read mentions is evidence, with the span. Only locations are judged — a code identifier or a number belongs to the hallucination signals — and the rule declines rather than guesses when a read was truncated.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Consistency of claims across repeated runs of one input is not evaluated.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: No cohort or baseline; only per-rule failure rates over time.

cells.question: Q2
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The fabrication detector is measured on its corpus; the judge templates are unmeasured until a user-supplied key runs the judge harness, and the page says pending until then.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Form is measured — length, sentence count, non-empty, and stub or placeholder markers — not whether the ask was answered.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: Coverage of an expected answer's terms is measured when one is supplied; nothing yet reads the structure of the ask to see which parts were answered.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: The trajectory against the one the caller expected: tool_sequence compares the calls made with expected_trajectory.tool_calls in a mode (strict, unordered, subset, superset, ordered_subset — the default, a two-pointer subsequence check), matching by name and, when the expectation names arguments, by exact or subset input; a policy, so it gates because the caller stated the expectation; measured with intervals. Which parts of the ASK were acted on, without an expectation to compare against, is still the judge's question.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Complete on most runs is readable as a case's pass rate over its repeats: compare_traces groups every evaluation of one case across runs and reports the case's pass rate with a 95% Wilson interval and a flaky flag, and the run-level rate by a cluster bootstrap over cases — of the composed verdict, not of this question alone; a per-question filter is not shipped, so the rate cannot be read for this question by itself.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Per-rule failure counts over time only.

cells.question: Q3
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The completeness rules are measured as conformance to their stated formula, and each result says so in its uncertainty basis rather than presenting the number as a detection rate.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Both relevance rules skip without the input; on a single output the question is unanswerable and the verdict's coverage says so.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: Lexical, three rules: the share of the input's content terms the output carries (keyword_overlap) and continuity of topic across sentences (topic_consistency) are measurements that score; answers_the_ask is the pair as a policy with no number of its own — when both fail at their thresholds the output answers something else and the verdict fails on policy_gate at the shipped defaults, and it skips whenever either measurement skips and on a one-term ask, so a one-word right answer is never a fire. Measured on the composite corpus before it existed: no classless clean case flipped, four of eight off-task cases caught (two too short to measure, two reuse the ask's words), six stub misses caught. A keyed helpfulness judge template exists and is unmeasured.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: The wrong tool for the ask, from the catalogue valid_tool_arguments already takes: tool_choice scores the ask's content terms against each tool's name, description and input property names (the relevance tokenizer) and fires when an uncalled tool fits the ask at least 0.5 and beats the union of the tools called by at least 0.34, naming both; judged over the whole trajectory so several tools that each serve part of the ask are not wrong; a heuristic detection, so it degrades the score and never vetoes; measured with intervals. Lexical: a tool whose description never mentions the ask's words is invisible to it.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: On-task on most runs is readable as a case's pass rate over its repeats: compare_traces groups every evaluation of one case across runs and reports the case's pass rate with a 95% Wilson interval and a flaky flag, and the run-level rate by a cluster bootstrap over cases — of the composed verdict, not of this question alone; a per-question filter is not shipped, so the rate cannot be read for this question by itself.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Per-rule failure counts over time only.

cells.question: Q4
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The relevance rules are measured as conformance to their lexical formula; the proof does not yet include cases where the formula and a reader would disagree.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: From the output alone, completion is a judgment: the task_completed judge template (0.15.0) reads the ask and the output — and the trajectory when the caller passes it — and scores whether the claims of completion are borne out. User-keyed; its measurement is pending until a key runs proof:judge, and the evaluators matrix says so.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: An ask that declares its parts — a bullet list, a numbered or lettered enumeration, a first/second/finally sequence — is checked part by part, and an unaddressed part is named with a span into the ask itself. A multi-part ask written as flowing prose is not split: a writer who numbers their questions is declaring separate things, and a full stop declares nothing.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: A part of the ask the answer never mentions may still have been DONE: ask_coverage (v2, 0.15.0) reads the trajectory and counts a part covered when a tool call the trace shows carries its terms — the same lexical test as the answer, so the trajectory can only add coverage (the rule needs the output and the ask; it reads the trajectory when the trace carries one). Recall-only for the family; what the trajectory does not carry is still unjudged, and the judge template above is the other half.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Completes the task seven of ten runs is readable for THIS question: compare_traces (and GET /api/v1/cases/:key) take `question: task_completed` and count only evaluations that judged it, an attempt passing when every rule answering it passed — a case's rate with a 95% Wilson interval, the flaky flag, and the run-level rate by a cluster bootstrap over cases, of the question rather than the composed verdict (0.15.0).

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: No cohort or baseline for completion: nothing ships that says what an agent, a run or a period usually completes, so a drop in completion has no reference to be a drop against. Named as the one open cell of this question.

cells.question: Q5
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The ask-coverage reading of completion — were the parts of the ask addressed — has a published family (precision and recall per rule at https://iris-eval.com/proof); no end-to-end task-completion evaluator exists, so nothing measures completion beyond that reading.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Acting well is a property of the trajectory, not of a single output.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: As for a single output.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: Three deterministic trajectory rules, each measured with intervals: a failed tool call the output never acknowledges, a repeated call with the same input, and a call whose arguments the tool’s own JSON Schema rejects and the agent never retried. Argument validity needs the tools catalogue; tool CHOICE — whether a valid call was the right one — is judged in the on-task row (Q4×S3, tool_choice).

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Acts well on most runs is readable as a case's pass rate over its repeats: compare_traces groups every evaluation of one case across runs and reports the case's pass rate with a 95% Wilson interval and a flaky flag, and the run-level rate by a cluster bootstrap over cases — of the composed verdict, not of this question alone; a per-question filter is not shipped, so the rate cannot be read for this question by itself.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Per-rule failure counts for the two trajectory rules over time only.

cells.question: Q6
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: Both trajectory rules are measured with intervals on their corpus families, and each fire carries its positive predictive value.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Trace cost and token usage are captured and judged by the cost bundle, and the evaluator's own spend — the judge's tokens and cost — is stored on the evaluation.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: A cost ceiling and a token ratio are judged from the trace totals; the ratio measures verbosity, not efficiency, and says so.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: A step budget is judged from the trajectory itself: max_steps fails a task that takes more tool calls than the deployment's ceiling, advising at the shipped default and gating once a deployment sets its own; step_budget fails a task that takes more than the budget the CALLER stated for it (expected_trajectory.step_budget, or the number of expected calls) times a tolerance, and gates because the caller stated it; no_tool_loop counts the repeated work inside either. Per-call tokens and cost are carried on a call and not yet read; the trace TOTAL is judged elsewhere in this row.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Cost across repeats of one input is readable only through the case's pass rate under the cost rules: compare_traces groups every evaluation of one case across runs and reports the case's pass rate with a 95% Wilson interval and a flaky flag, and the run-level rate by a cluster bootstrap over cases — of the composed verdict, not of this question alone; a per-question filter is not shipped, so the rate cannot be read for this question by itself. No rule reads an agent's own cost distribution.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Aggregate cost over a time window is served to the dashboard, and a trace is judged against the agent's own cost distribution: the cost_anomaly rule and the cost-spike moment read the modified z over the agent's last 200 costed traces (median and MAD), never a fixed dollar line.

cells.question: Q7
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The cost rules are measured as conformance to their formula, and the evaluator's own spend is stored per evaluation.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Better or worse than before needs at least two things to compare.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: As for a single output.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: A trajectory regression shows as its rule failing more often between two runs, reported per rule, worst first, once traces are logged with tool calls and a run id. The trajectories themselves are not compared step by step.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Evaluations of the same case across runs are grouped by case key and reported as a per-case pass rate with a 95% interval; a case answered both ways is reported as flaky. The run-level rate is a cluster bootstrap over cases, so ten repeats of one question are not counted as ten questions.

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Two runs are compared on pass rate with a 95% interval on the difference; when the runs share case keys they are paired and the discordant cases are tested exactly. When the evidence cannot exclude "no change" it says so and reports the smallest change that many cases could have detected. Runs measuring different things are refused unless forced, naming what differs. Scores bucketed over time still feed the drift view, and a CUSUM per agent and rule watches the stream itself: a regression-alarm moment marks the evaluation at which a rule's fail rate crossed a line derived for an in-control run length of about 500, reporting and never gating. The discordant cases are listed with both evaluations and the rules that flipped, and a run can be pinned as the baseline every later run is compared against (PATCH /api/v1/runs/:id; an omitted before means the baseline).

cells.question: Q8
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: The verdict a gate keys on is measured on a composite corpus, and a candidate composer is scored beside the shipped one with an interval on the difference and a held-out split, so a change to the composer is measured before it ships. On a deployment’s own traces the same question is answerable directly: re-scoring a run under the current rules writes the new verdicts into a new run marked as a re-evaluation, and comparing the two isolates the rules change — the executions are identical, so any difference is the evaluator.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Every fired detection carries typed evidence — offsets into the raw output, never a paraphrase — and a message naming the pattern; the stored evaluation reads back the same way.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: The grounded signals name the contradiction they found; measurements carry their value, unit and the threshold they were held to and where it came from.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: A silent tool failure names the failed call by index, why it failed and what the output claimed instead; a loop names every repeated call and the threshold.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Where it fails across repeats: a case answered both ways is reported as flaky, least reliable first. compare_traces groups every evaluation of one case across runs and reports the case's pass rate with a 95% Wilson interval and a flaky flag, and the run-level rate by a cluster bootstrap over cases — of the composed verdict, not of this question alone; a per-question filter is not shipped, so the rate cannot be read for this question by itself.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Top failures over a window are served to the dashboard; the held-out check is 24 staged transcripts from one agent on one repository, reported without an interval; there is no sample of unstaged production traffic.

cells.question: Q9
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: Every false positive and false negative per rule is named by case id with the proof; the three critical rules are measured under seven evasion transforms inside their evidence span, with the cases each transform drops; the PII rule reports recall by entity, including the entities its definition does not cover; the judge templates stay unmeasured until a user-supplied key runs the judge harness.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S1
cells.summary: Every rule result carries what kind of claim it is, what it saw, where in the raw text it found it, and how wrong it tends to be; the verdict names which layer decided — a configured policy, a high-precision detector, a check that could not answer, or the combined risk against the deployment's stated loss ratio — and one definition of passed covers the deterministic rules, the judge and the citation verifier alike.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S2
cells.summary: The verdict names which layer decided it and which rules did the deciding, coverage says which evaluation questions were judged and which input was missing for the rest, and a critical check that was asked and could not answer makes the verdict unknown rather than clean — a state a gate can fail closed on, and a setting the deployment chooses. Every rule deploy, delete, toggle and update and every trace deletion is recorded in an audit log the agent can read, so a rule changed or evidence removed around a verdict can be found afterwards.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S3
cells.summary: When tool calls are absent the trajectory rules skip and coverage names the question as unjudged; both rules are non-critical by default, so their skip never vetoes.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S4
cells.summary: Trust over repeats is a case's pass rate with a 95% Wilson interval and a flaky flag, and a run-level rate by a cluster bootstrap over cases so ten repeats of one question are not ten questions; the interval is the trust statement. No composer votes over repeats — the rate is reported, not turned into one verdict — and the judge has no repeat harness.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S5
cells.summary: Population-level trust: two windows are compared with both denominators and a 95% interval on the difference in pass rate, shown on the dashboard's change banner; two runs are compared with a Newcombe interval on the difference (McNemar on the discordant pairs when the cases pair). An interval that straddles zero is reported as not distinguishable, with the sample that would distinguish it. The deployment's own labels on a rule's fires say how often those fires were right on its traffic, with a Wilson interval; at twenty labels that number is in force on every verdict (the risk estimate reads it in place of the published one), the prior is estimated from the rule's fire rate, and the rule whose next label narrows the most uncertainty is named.

cells.question: Q10
cells.subject: S6
cells.summary: Precision, recall and intervals per rule are published and reproducible with one command, served to agents as a resource and on every rule result as its uncertainty; beside them, what a fire is worth at field prevalence, a credible interval that does not collapse at zero errors, the verdict’s own accuracy on a composite corpus, conformance of every custom rule type to its definition, and a matrix that asks thirteen trust questions of every evaluator and answers each cell from the proof files; the corpus is model-labelled until the blind human label lands, and every number says so.

questions.text: is it safe
is it grounded / correct
is it complete
is it on-task
did it complete the task
did it act well (tool choice, arguments, efficiency)
what did it cost

clients.about: Every MCP client Iris names as a place it runs, one row each. A row is `verified` when a test in this repository drives that client's real integration surface on every CI run. A row is `claimed` when the installer writes the configuration shape the client's own documentation describes and that writer is tested on the shape — but nobody on the Iris side has watched that client connect. No client is called supported without a row. Locked by tests/clients-contract.test.ts: the rows are exactly the installer's profiles, each row's source is the page its profile was written from, every evidence path exists, every source is a URL with the date it was last read, and the README and the site render their client lists from these rows.

rows.config: `~/.claude.json` (user scope, `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set), an `mcpServers` block beside Claude Code's own settings; the capture plugin installs from the repository's plugin marketplace
rows.name: Claude Code
rows.summary: On every CI run, on Linux, macOS and Windows, the installer from this commit's packed tarball writes the entry and the real `claude` CLI starts Iris from it: `claude mcp list` reports it Connected and `claude mcp get` shows it at user scope; uninstall takes it out again. The capture plugin's three hooks (UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop) are driven through the real hook scripts with the payload shapes Claude Code documents, ending in a real ingest read back from the store. What is not verified by a test: a model session calling the tools.

rows.config: `claude_desktop_config.json` in the Claude application-data directory, an `mcpServers` block
rows.name: Claude Desktop
rows.summary: The installer writes the `mcpServers` entry into a dedicated JSON file at the path Claude Desktop documents, keeping existing servers; the writer is tested on that shape. No test launches Claude Desktop.

rows.config: `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (or a workspace `.cursor/mcp.json`), an `mcpServers` block with `"type": "stdio"`, which Cursor's field table marks required; a one-click install link on the site
rows.name: Cursor
rows.summary: The installer writes the `mcpServers` entry, `type` included, into `mcp.json` as Cursor's documentation describes; the writer is tested on that shape. No test launches Cursor: its connection could not be driven headlessly here, so it stays claimed.

rows.config: `mcp_config.json` in `~/.config/devin/` (`%APPDATA%\devin\` on Windows), an `mcpServers` block — Windsurf became Devin Desktop, and its documentation now names this file
rows.name: Devin Desktop (Windsurf)
rows.summary: The installer writes the `mcpServers` entry into `mcp_config.json` at the path Devin Desktop's documentation (formerly Windsurf's) names; the writer is tested on that shape. No test launches Devin Desktop.

rows.config: `~/.continue/mcpServers/iris-eval.json`, a file of its own in Continue's MCP folder, an `mcpServers` block
rows.name: Continue
rows.summary: The installer writes its own `iris-eval.json` into Continue's global `mcpServers` folder, which Continue's documentation says accepts the Claude Desktop JSON format; the writer is tested on that shape. No test launches Continue.

rows.config: `mcp.json` in the VS Code user directory (or `.vscode/mcp.json` in a workspace), a `servers` block — VS Code's own key, not `mcpServers`
rows.name: VS Code
rows.summary: The installer writes under `servers`, the key VS Code's native MCP support documents, and uninstalls only its own entry; the writer is tested on that shape. No test launches VS Code.

rows.config: `~/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json`, shared by Cline in VS Code, JetBrains and the CLI, an `mcpServers` block
rows.name: Cline
rows.summary: The installer writes the `mcpServers` entry into `cline_mcp_settings.json` where Cline's configuration documentation puts it; the writer is tested on that shape. No test launches Cline.

rows.name: Zed
rows.summary: The installer writes the `context_servers` entry in the shape Zed's documentation shows, into the settings file with its comments kept; the writer is tested on that shape, including the comment header Zed writes. No test launches Zed.

rows.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
rows.summary: The installer writes an `[mcp_servers.iris-eval]` TOML table as the Codex MCP documentation describes; the writer is tested on that shape. No test launches Codex.

rows.name: Gemini CLI
rows.summary: On every CI run, on Linux, macOS and Windows, the installer from this commit's packed tarball writes the entry and the real `gemini` CLI starts Iris from it: `gemini mcp list` reports it Connected in a trusted folder; uninstall takes it out again. No model call is made. What is not verified by a test: a model session calling the tools.

questions.text: Is the output safe to show — no leaked personal data or credentials, no injection, nothing the deployment prohibits?
Is the output grounded in what the agent was given or read, rather than invented?
Did the agent produce a full answer rather than a stub, a fragment or a promise?
Is the output on task — does it address what was asked?
Did the task actually complete, as opposed to reading as if it had?
Did the agent act well — the right tools, valid arguments, no loops, failures acknowledged?
Did the run cost what the deployment allows, in money and tokens?
Is this agent better or worse than before, with an interval?
Where does it fail, and why?
Can this verdict be trusted — how often is each evaluator wrong?

evaluators.about: The thirteen trust questions asked of every evaluator Iris ships; every cell derived from the committed proof files by scripts/claims/generators/evaluators.mjs, never typed. steps: Get an API key from Anthropic or OpenAI.

Put it in the environment of the process that runs Iris, not only your shell. Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and most MCP clients: the "env" block of the iris-eval entry in your MCP config — "iris-eval": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@iris-eval/mcp-server"], "env": { "IRIS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-ant-..." } } (IRIS_OPENAI_API_KEY for an OpenAI key). Docker: -e IRIS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... on the run command. HTTP or CI: export it before starting iris-eval.
Restart the MCP session. A running process never sees a variable set after it started.

Confirm from inside your client: read iris://capabilities — judge.enabled must be true there. A key exported in your shell is not passed to the process your client spawns unless its config lists it. On a machine, `npx @iris-eval/mcp-server --self-test` prints the judge line for that shell, and GET /api/v1/health reports judge.enabled on a running dashboard.

Spend guard: each call is capped by IRIS_LLM_JUDGE_MAX_COST_USD_PER_EVAL (default 0.25 USD) and refused before any spend if the worst case would exceed it. Iris calls the provider directly with your key and never proxies it.
enable.title: Enable the LLM judge (optional; the deterministic rules never need it)

maintenance.method: GitHub REST /repos/iris-eval/mcp-server/issues, unauthenticated; pull requests excluded; hours = closed_at minus created_at; median and p75 by linear interpolation between order statistics; window = issues whose closed_at falls in the last 90 days.

confidence.rule: decisive needs the credible interval to exclude τ AND, in the verdict's tenth of p_bad, the dev split to hold at least 10 risk-decided verdicts from at least 4 distinct detector-firing patterns, their observed bad rate to be consistent with the stated p_bad (mean predicted inside its Wilson 95% interval), and that interval to lie wholly on the verdict's side of τ; otherwise marginal (src/eval/confidence.ts)

difference.reads: accuracy(risk variant) − accuracy(legacy); an interval that excludes zero on the positive side says the variant is more accurate on this corpus; one that straddles zero says the corpus cannot tell them apart

method.calibration: Brier score and expected calibration error over ten equal-width bins; the legacy score read as P(bad) = 1 − score, the risk as p_bad
method.legacy: the pre-0.10.0 arithmetic, computed explicitly by proof/lib/legacy-composer.ts: weighted score ≥ the default threshold and no critical failure. From 0.10.0 the engine composes passed, so this baseline is derived rather than read off the result; from 0.12.0 it is no longer a product behaviour and this file is the only place it survives

priorModes.per-class: π is the prior that each examined class is present, as originally specified; with K classes examined the prior that nothing is wrong is (1 − π)^K
priorModes.per-output: π is the prior that the output is bad; spread over the K examined classes as π_c = 1 − (1 − π)^(1/K)

method.risk: class-grouped noisy-OR over the published positive predictive values at the stated prior (max within a class; residual miss rate when nothing fired); 2,000 seeded draws over the Beta posteriors for the interval; gates and vetoes before the risk; measurements and policies never enter (src/eval/risk.ts, the module the product uses)
method.shouldShip: by construction (any tier-A class present → false) unless a human label overrides; cases with shouldShip null are excluded from accuracy
method.split: fnv1a(id + "iris-composite-split-v1") % 100 < 70 → dev, else test; never stored

sweep.note: utility = −(false blocks + c × missed blocks) at c = 1 on the dev split; the argmax is a check on the loss model, never adopted

custom.method: each custom rule type built by createCustomRule under the family's config and run on cases labelled by its documented definition; a disagreement is a rule defect or a definition error, never an opinion

entities.method: positives carry `entities` named by the case author; caught = the rule failed the case for any reason; named = the evidence named this entity; recall = named / present, Wilson 95% — a case caught for another reason is visible as caught − named

humanAgreement.note: founder blind label of a 140-case stratified sample (twenty per judgment family); until then the labels are same-model dual annotation (see proof/README.md)

judge.note: run npm run proof:judge with a judge API key, or dispatch the proof-judge workflow

latency.method: EvalEngine.evaluateAll — the call evaluate_output makes — over every case in the proof corpus, 25 warm-up runs discarded, storage excluded

method.ppvAt: positive predictive value of a fire at prevalences 0.01, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5: sens·π / (sens·π + (1 − spec)(1 − π)) from this family's counts
method.skipped: a skipped result (the rule declined to judge) counts as not failed; the count is reported per rule

transcripts.method: each transcript runs through the real engine exactly as evaluate_output does, at the shipped defaults. BUNDLE verdicts are compared to the answer key written when the transcript was captured; the SHIP verdict is compared to "no failure class is present"; CLASSES CAUGHT counts the classes a person said were present that some rule declaring that class actually failed on. The three are different questions and the class number is the one that stays meaningful as rules are added, because it needs no relabelling. Gaps are MEASURED here and read by tests/real-transcripts.test.ts, so a gap that closes cannot stay recorded as open

transforms.method: for each positive the rule caught untransformed with a span into raw text — the agent output, or a tool output for a trajectory rule — the text inside every reported span is transformed and the rule re-run; recall = still fails / applicable cases, Wilson 95%; a case the rule missed in the clear, or a span the transform does not apply to, is not counted. Rebuilding a tool output clears the derived step list, or the rule would read the untransformed calls through stepsOf and the number would mean nothing

transforms.describe: a zero-width space (U+200B) inserted at the middle of the span
every Latin a e o p c x (and capitals) inside the span replaced by its Cyrillic lookalike
every ASCII letter and digit inside the span replaced by its fullwidth form (NFKC folds it back)
every space inside the span replaced by a no-break space (U+00A0)
a tab inserted at the middle of the span
a line break inserted at the middle of the span
the case of every ASCII letter inside the span swapped

release.currentReleaseHeadline: Honest numbers, a lighter footprint, nothing done silently
